editorNote: Disclosure clocks and data exposure dominate: Google shortens its bug-reporting grace period, a researcher counts leaky AI-built apps, PyPI makes provenance visible, and a court lets the DRAM price-fixing suit proceed.

stories.headline: Project Zero moves to 'Full 90' disclosure, with the window shrinking to 30 days by 2028
stories.summary: Google's Project Zero is replacing its 90+30 policy with 'Full X', disclosing a bug X days after it is reported: Full 90 from Nov. 13, Full 60 from Feb. 2, 2027, and Full 30 from Jan. 3, 2028. It cites AI-assisted discovery and exploitation, and drops most special cases, including the grace period and severity as a factor.
stories.whyItMatters: Vendors lose the extra 30-day patch-adoption window now and face a progressively shorter clock after that.

stories.headline: Researchers find Lovable-built apps sending database records, including passport details, to unauthenticated visitors
stories.summary: Crissy Field GmbH analyzed 159,041 Lovable projects; of 34,545 using Supabase, 24,664 sent database records on page load. Exposed data included over 200,000 chat messages from one forum and over 1,000 records with passport details; the authors caution that their 30% email-table figure is not a confirmed leak rate and the sample is unrepresentative.
stories.whyItMatters: Lovable's terms put application security on customers, so apps generated with AI can ship with exposed data unless someone checks.

stories.headline: Court denies motion to dismiss DRAM price-fixing suit against Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron
stories.summary: On Nov. 14 Judge Noël Wise (N.D. Cal.) found the complaint plausibly alleges a Sherman Act agreement to cut conventional DRAM output and shift capacity to HBM. The allegations are unproven; defendants must answer by Dec. 7, with a case management conference on Jan. 12, 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: The case survives where an earlier suit against the same companies (DRAM II) was dismissed, moving to discovery on the three firms, which allegedly hold over 91% of DRAM revenue.

sourceLinks.title: LitNews: DRAM conspiracy suit survives dismissal

stories.headline: PyPI's redesigned project pages add a Security tab and provenance warnings
stories.summary: Each release now shows full or no provenance, with per-file attestations and four warning types: incomplete, inconsistent, change of, and loss of provenance. Release files get search and filtering, and late uploads are flagged; PyPI notes that no provenance does not necessarily mean a release is malicious.
stories.whyItMatters: Unusual publishing patterns are now flagged on the page itself rather than requiring users to inspect attestations.
